mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship: compare the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR in the RECENT_5 window against the same ratio in the ALL_PRIOR window for Team A. A large drop in the ratio signals a regime where volume is maintained but accuracy has collapsed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the shots_on_target/shots ratio in RECENT_5 falls substantially below the ALL_PRIOR ratio for the same team, that team's goal output in the same RECENT_5 window is suppressed relative to its ALL_PRIOR goal average — i.e. shot-accuracy regime and goal output move together beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target production has diverged sharply downward in recent matches relative to its long-run average, while its shots volume has declined only modestly. This divergence between shot volume and shot accuracy (shots vs shots-on-target, recent vs all-prior) jointly characterises a conversion-quality regime shift that neither observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) and computing their ratio across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; the engine would need to evaluate the interaction between volume and accuracy trends.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's RECENT_5 possession FOR is below its ALL_PRIOR possession FOR AND its RECENT_5 shots AGAINST exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots AGAINST. Test whether goals conceded also rises in this joint condition relative to either condition alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team simultaneously shows reduced possession and elevated shots conceded in recent matches, its goals-against rate rises more than either signal predicts independently — i.e. the joint condition amplifies defensive vulnerability beyond additive effects.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's defensive exposure has increased sharply in recent matches (shots against and shots_on_target against both up in RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR), while its possession has dropped and goals conceded have risen. The joint relationship between a team's recent possession deficit, its defensive shot-volume conceded, and its goals-against rate captures a multi-dimensional defensive vulnerability regime not reducible to any single observable.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (possession deficit AND shots-against elevation) simultaneously, which is structurally richer than any single-observable or single-band split the engine already covers.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's corners AGAINST (what Team A allows) and Team B's corners FOR (what Team B generates), comparing both against the competition context baseline. The mechanism tests whether the cross-team pairing of a high-corners-allowed team (A) with a low-corners-generated team (B) produces a corner total that diverges from what either team's individual profile or the competition baseline would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's corners-against average substantially exceeds the competition mean AND Team B's corners-for average is at or below the competition mean, the total corners in the match are suppressed relative to what Team A's corners-against profile alone would predict — i.e. the two-sided asymmetry jointly constrains the outcome.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates significantly more corners against it than the competition average, while Team B concedes far fewer corners than the competition average. The asymmetric corner-kick profile — one team that structurally yields many corners FOR its opponent versus one that structurally suppresses corners against — creates a joint cross-team corner imbalance that is not captured by either team's individual corner observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship involving two distinct observable perspectives (Team A's corners-against vs Team B's corners-for) simultaneously benchmarked against a competition baseline. It is not a single observable with one band; it requires the joint evaluation of both sides' profiles against each other.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half-level split of corners FOR for each team: compare first-half vs second-half corner averages for Team A and Team B separately. The mechanism tests whether the directional asymmetry (Team A back-loaded, Team B front-loaded) predicts which half produces more total corners, and whether the second-half corner total diverges from the first-half total in a direction consistent with Team A's acceleration and Team B's deceleration.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's corners-for rate rises from first to second half while the opponent's falls, the second half total corners are driven more by the accelerating team, and the within-match distribution of corners is skewed toward the half where the accelerating team dominates — i.e. the asymmetric half-profiles jointly predict the intra-match corner distribution.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of corner kicks for both teams reveals whether corner generation is front-loaded (first half) or back-loaded (second half). Team A's corners-for split (2.21 first half vs 2.57 second half) and Team B's corners-for split (2.60 first half vs 2.07 second half) show opposite intra-match temporal profiles. The joint interaction of these two asymmetric half-level corner profiles — one team accelerating, one decelerating — is a within-match state mechanism not captured by full-match totals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires within-match half-level resolution and the joint evaluation of two teams' half-split profiles simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band; it combines half-period conditioning with a cross-team asymmetric comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's RECENT_5 fouls AGAINST (fouls suffered, elevated) and Team A's RECENT_5 yellow_cards FOR (elevated) relative to their ALL_PRIOR baselines. Test whether the second-half cards total (cards_2h) is elevated in matches where both conditions hold simultaneously, compared to matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent fouls-suffered rate and its own yellow-card rate are both elevated above their long-run averages simultaneously, the second-half card count in those matches rises more than either signal alone predicts — i.e. the joint disciplinary pressure regime amplifies second-half card accumulation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's fouls committed have risen sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5: 11.2 vs ALL_PRIOR: 12.45 — modest, but fouls against Team A have spiked to 15.4 vs 11.83 ALL_PRIOR), while Team A's yellow cards FOR have also risen in RECENT_5. The joint relationship between a team's recent fouls-against (fouls suffered) and its own yellow-card accumulation rate — two distinct observables — captures a disciplinary pressure regime: when a team is being fouled heavily AND accumulating more yellows itself, the second-half card environment is elevated beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two time windows, and linking them to a third observable (cards_2h) at half-level resolution. It is not reducible to any single observable with one band.
